identity.note: UFC athlete page: Alex Pereira (Poatan), Sao Bernardo do Campo, Brazil, age 38, listed at heavyweight, former UFC middleweight and light heavyweight champion and former Glory two-division champion; matches Glory, Wikipedia and Boxerbook (Brazil, born 1987, 194 cm).

wrestling.note: No wrestling background mentioned on the UFC page or Wikipedia; UWW database not searched, so not marked none_found.

grappling.note: Only talk of proposed grappling matches (challenge to Anthony Smith, mooted bout with Khamzat Chimaev) with no results; ADCC records not searched.

claims.text: Kayla Harrison, a two-time Olympic judo champion, presented him with a judo yellow belt after his UFC 303 title defence, following a promise tied to a throw she had taught him; an informal training-partner award, not a federation grade.
claims.level_note: Informal judo yellow belt (kyu grade) from a training partner; no competition record.

judo.note: Only an informal yellow belt given by training partner Kayla Harrison after UFC 303; no competitive judo record. JudoInside search failed to load, so a competition record could not be ruled out.

claims.text: Took the Glory middleweight world title from Simon Marcus by unanimous decision at Glory 46 in Guangzhou, China, on 14 October 2017.
Combat Press independently reports his unanimous-decision win over Simon Marcus for the Glory middleweight title at Glory 46 on 14 October 2017.
Won the Glory interim light heavyweight title by third-round left-hook knockout of Donegi Abena at Glory 68 in Miami on 28 September 2019, while still holding the middleweight belt.
His UFC profile lists a professional kickboxing record of 33 wins and 7 losses with 21 knockouts.
Wikipedia says he took silver at the 2013 WAKO amateur world championships in Guaruja, Brazil, at -91 kg; the WAKO site did not show individual results to confirm it.

sources_checked.name: WAKO Guaruja 2013 medals and results post

kickboxing.note: Glory titles confirmed by Glory's own news pages and independently by Combat Press. The Glory fighter page shows a Glory-only 12-4 record alongside a 33-7 career figure, which reflects Glory versus whole-career totals. The 2013 WAKO world silver is Wikipedia-only: the WAKO results post for Guaruja 2

claims.text: Wikipedia lists one professional boxing bout, a third-round TKO win over Marcelo de Souza Cruz in Sorocaba, Brazil, in June 2017, for a 1-0 record.

boxing.note: First pass said none_found, but Wikipedia reports one pro boxing bout. BoxRec blocked automated access (HTTP 403). Boxerbook has an entry for this Alex Pereira (Brazil, born 1987) but shows no record, so the bout is unconfirmed.

claims.text: Coach Plinio Cruz awarded him a BJJ brown belt in November 2022, a few days after he won the UFC middleweight title at UFC 281.
He was promoted to BJJ black belt by his coaches right after his UFC 300 knockout of Jamahal Hill in April 2024, with coach Plinio Cruz announcing it.
FloGrappling reports his BJJ black belt promotion around UFC 300 in April 2024 and names Glover Teixeira among the coaches behind it.

bjj.note: Brown and black belt promotions are reported by reputable outlets, but there is no federation or lineage record, so the belt is not verified. Sources differ on who promoted him to black belt: BJJEE and Wikipedia credit Plinio Cruz, while FloGrappling credits his coaches including Glover Teixeira.

sambo.note: No sambo background mentioned in any page read; FIAS records not searched.
